title: Strawman: Request Threads and Actionable Sprint Lanes
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a strawman synthesis of recent customer feedback threads (Aug–Oct 2026) with a pragmatic translation into sprintable lanes and low-effort probes. The goal: move a set of high-frequency asks from backlog fuzz to ownerable workstreams we can ship in 1–3 sprints.

Notes on provenance:
- Sources: support tickets, CS calls (recordings), AE debriefs, field notes from Solutions Eng (see linked Confluence).
- Signal density: the three themes below represent ~62% of recurring asks and ~78% of high-severity escalations for dedicated/private customers.

Executive summary (one-paragraph):
Customers repeatedly ask for clearer cost attribution, faster mitigation controls for latency spikes, and safer, observable routing fallbacks. These are not single features — they’re cross-cutting controls that touch API surface, Console UI, and runtime defaults. Proposed approach: break into three sprint lanes (Billing & Transparency, Operational Controls, Eval & Quality Safety) with 1 low-effort probe per lane to demonstrate value in 2 weeks, and a 1–3 sprint deliverable for full rollouts.

Top themes and representative customer quotes:
1) Cost attribution and token-level clarity
   - "We need to know which endpoint call and which user generated this $1200 bill spike." — large SaaS customer
   - Asks: per-route/per-api-key token breakdown, exportable CSVs, and alerting when spend deviates for a route.

2) Operational controls for graceful degradation
   - "When the LLM has fallback latency, our UI freezes — we need automatic degraded responses or short-circuit options." — fintech customer
   - Asks: per-route timeout and fallback model policies, canary to cheaper model when KPIs exceed threshold, sticky caching for prefixes.

3) Observability and deterministic troubleshooting
   - "We keep chasing nondeterministic latency spikes; we need the trace that joins API call -> worker kernel -> quantization variant." — platform team
   - Asks: token-level latency histograms, traceable runtime variant (quantized vs full), KV cache hit rates surfaced per request.

Prioritization matrix (impact x effort) — quick take:
- High impact / low effort: Per-route spend export, API-side per-request tag to attach product-user metadata (low-effort SDK + export).
- High impact / medium effort: Per-route fallback policies (need runtime + control-plane UI).
- High impact / high effort: Per-token latency traces joined to worker-level diagnostics (needs sampling, trace storage, SRE involvement).
- Medium impact / low effort: Quick UX tweak — surfacing billing alerts in Console (prototype in 1 week).

Proposed sprint lanes (owner, probe, 2-week outcome, 1–3 sprint deliverable):
A) Billing & Transparency (owner: Marcus Reed)
   - Probe: Add a per-route CSV export for last-30-day token usage behind a feature flag; wire to an S3 location for customers to download.
   - 2-week outcome: customers get CSV with route/api_key, date, tokens_in, tokens_out, model_name. We solicit feedback from 3 pilot customers.
   - 1–3 sprint deliverable: Permanent Console pane with per-key spend, alerting (thresholds + webhook), and mapping from SDK metadata tag -> product user.

B) Operational Controls & Fallbacks (owner: Arjun Patel)
   - Probe: Add a simple per-route policy that defines a fallback candidate model and a 200ms soft-timeout that returns a stub or shorter completion. Expose as an API flag.
   - 2-week outcome: trial with two customers, verify decreased UI timeouts and reduced visible errors.
   - 1–3 sprint deliverable: Full control-plane UX for policy creation, CLA logic for canaries (percent traffic shift), and server-side safe defaults for Dedicated/Private installs.

C) Observability & Diagnostics (owner: Sophie Nguyen)
   - Probe: Sample 1% of requests and emit a lightweight trace with: route, model_variant, kernel_id, kv_cache_hit_rate, total_token_latency. Store traces in existing tracing backend.
   - 2-week outcome: internal SREs can reproduce a recent spike with trace joins; customer pilot can view sampled traces.
   - 1–3 sprint deliverable: Rollout configurable sampling, token-level histograms in Console, and a developer-mode trace link in API responses for traced requests.

Detailed asks translated to tickets (candidate):
- JIRA-7129: "Per-route token export CLI + Console link" (probe: CSV export).
- JIRA-7184: "Per-route fallback policy (soft-timeout + model candidate)" (probe: API flag).
- JIRA-7232: "Lightweight sampled runtime traces (1% default)" (SRE + infra).

Acceptance criteria (how we know it worked):
- Billing probe: pilot customers confirm CSV maps to their internal billing and can identify a spend anomaly within 2 clicks.
- Fallback probe: customers observe fewer UI timeouts in monitored sessions and a reduction in P0 incidents over a 2-week pilot.
- Observability probe: SRE can reproduce at least 2 historical spikes using sample traces. Customer pilot can access trace view for sampled request ids.

Potential risks and mitigations:
- Risk: exposing too much runtime internals (kernel ids, quantization variants) could overwhelm customers or create support churn.
  Mitigation: start with high-level labels ("quantized-v1", "fp16-optim") and only add low-level diagnostics under developer-mode.
- Risk: sampling traces at scale increases storage/cost.
  Mitigation: strict sampling defaults (0.5–1%), retention TTL 7 days by default, and opt-in higher retention per enterprise contract.
- Risk: Customers want immediate per-user mapping for billing but integrating with product-level IDs is messy.
  Mitigation: ship SDK metadata tags quickly and document best-practice mapping patterns for customers.

Low-effort UX patterns (fast wins):
- Add a small "billing anomaly" CTA in Console that links to exported CSV and suggested next steps (escalate, set threshold, open ticket).
- Add a toggle to turn on per-route fallback for a limited set of models.
- Add a sampled-trace badge to Console logs to mark when a trace exists for a request id.

Customer pilot candidates (initial outreach):
- Fintech alpha (high tolerance for Canary experiments; strong need for timeouts) — contact: Alex Ramos (AE).
- E-commerce platform (heavy embedding usage; wants billing granularity) — contact: Priya Singh (CS lead).
- Platform integrator (observability-first; willing to test traces) — contact: Daniel K.

Open questions for Product & SRE sync:
- What quota limits do we place on CSV export frequency?
- Can we reuse the existing tracing pipeline or do we need a lightweight sidecar emitter?
- What safeguards do we need for fallback policies to avoid model-regression loops?

Next steps (concrete):
1) Marcus to spin a minimal CSV export prototype and share with pilot customers by 2026-11-16 (JIRA-7129).
2) Arjun to implement fallback API flag in sandbox and draft a policy schema by 2026-11-12 (JIRA-7184).
3) Sophie to add a sampled trace emitter (0.5%) and a Console flag to view traces; SRE to validate reproduction by 2026-11-24 (JIRA-7232).
4) CS to prepare 3 pilot customers and schedule cadence for feedback demos (owner: Lila).

Appendix: quick fragments pulled from customer threads (verbatim samples)
- "We had a sudden $13k spike last month — no idea whether it was a bug or a bot. If we had per-route breakdown we could have caught it earlier."
- "If the model is slow, show the last cached completion and surface that you used a fallback model — better than nothing."
- "I love the streaming API but I need an easy way to know which model variant served which tokens for post-hoc debugging."

References and reading list:
- Confluence: CS / Signal Archive / 9482 (linked above)
- Prior art: github.com/redwood-inference/console-billing-proto (internal prototype)
- Related tickets: JIRA-6102 (billing anomalies doc), JIRA-6830 (model-routing failsafe)

Notes to reviewers:
- This draft intentionally prioritizes pragmatic shipping (low-friction probes) over fully-baked product specs. Please flag major gaps, suggested owners, or any legal/compliance concerns for Private deployments.
- Callout: Dedicated and Private customers will need on-prem configuration knobs; ensure SRE and Private-Deployments eng are looped in if we progress.

-- Lila (CS)
